theory.title: Be supposed to, had better and ought to
theory.explanation: Use be supposed to for rules, expectations or arrangements. Use had better + base verb for strong advice, often when there may be a negative result. Use ought to + base verb for advice or what is morally right.
theory.tip: Be supposed to = se espera / está previsto. Had better = más vale. Ought to = debería.

content.passage: When Emma visited the clinic, the receptionist explained the rules. Patients are supposed to arrive ten minutes early and bring their appointment details. Emma had a bad headache, so the nurse said she had better rest and drink water. The doctor added that she ought to take regular breaks from screens. Visitors are also supposed to wash their hands before entering the treatment area.

items.prompt: Explain what patients are supposed to do before an appointment.
items.modelAnswer: I think looking after your health is about building realistic habits and making balanced choices. I try to stay active, drink enough water and get regular sleep. When I feel stressed, I take a break or go for a walk. It is important to follow medical advice and ask questions when something is unclear. Small changes can make a big difference over time, especially when people keep practising them.

content.audioTranscript: A: Have you got your appointment tomorrow? B: Yes, I want to talk about my daily routine. A: Are you doing enough exercise? B: I'm trying to. The doctor gave me some useful advice. A: What did they suggest? B: Drinking more water and getting enough sleep. A: Do you need any medicine? B: No, but I need to rest during my recovery. A: I hope you feel better by tomorrow.
